3. In the meantime the said lands were wrongly listed as vested property. Pritimoyee filed Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 1979 (Sat) before the Additional Deputy Commissioner, Satkhira. The -said A.D.C. by his order dated 26.2.84 recommended to the Board of Land Administration for releasing the said lands from the list of vested property. 

 4. Besides persuing her case before the revenue authorities Pritimoyee and others went to the civil court by instituting Title Suit No. 23 of 1983 against the Government of Bangladesh and others in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Satkhira, for declaration of title to the said lands, but allowed the suit to be dismissed for default by the order dated 2.5.85 obviously after getting information that the Board of Land Administration had accepted the recommendation of the A.D.C. for releasing the said lands from the list of vested property. However, presumely as advised Pritimayee filed Miscellaneous Case No. 52 of 1984 for setting aside the order of dis-missal of her suit. Then she received the memo. No. 1421/1 (3)-V. P.326/84 dated 14.5.85 from the Board of Land Administration containing its decision, that the said lands be released from the list of vested property. Naturally she also allowed the said miscellaneous case dis-missed for default on 6.8.92. 

 9. We have already stated the entire facts necessary for the disposal of the appeal and we need not repeat them. Order 47, Rule 1 of the Court of Civil Procedure which is applicable in a writ proceeding enjoins the learned Judges amongst others to review their own judgments or orders on the reason of mistake or error on the face of the record. The instant case was the best case in this respect.  We find, where the learned Judges ought to have exercised their review power. The reason upon which the review application was rejected must be held to be unconscionable and erroneous and so also was the memo of the Ministry of Land impugned in the writ petition. We, therefore, come to the conclusion that the High Court Division ought to have allowed the review application and ultimately it ought to have declared the impugned memo of the Ministry of Land as illegal, without lawful authority and of no legal effect. 

 10. In view of the legal position as concluded by us it will be an idle ceremony as well as injurious to the appellants for no fault of their own if we follow the usual course of remanding the writ petition for its disposal by the High Court Division. In the case of Naziruddin V. Hameeda Banu reported in 45 DLR (AD) 38, this Division explained the scope of Article 104 of the Constitution as hereunder: "It is an extraordinary procedure for doing justice for completion of or putting an end to a cause or matter pending before this court. If a substantial justice under law and on undisputed facts can be made so that parties may not be pushed to further litigation then a recourse to the provision of Art. 104 may be justified." 

 11. We find that the instant case fits with the principle as laid down in the reported case and accordingly this appeal is disposed of.
